description: Delinea (enterprise PAM leader, PE-backed by TPG/Thoma Bravo) acquired StrongDM (just-in-time runtime authorization for AI agents) on March 5, 2026, creating a unified identity security control plane covering human and non-human identities, AI agents, and privileged infrastructure access.
agents: Manages privileged access for AI agents in enterprise environments
Real-time policy evaluation and enforcement for autonomous non-human identities (NHIs)
Just-in-time access for AI agents across infrastructure, databases, containers, CI/CD
Delinea Iris AI drives policy recommendations and anomaly detection

funding.total: ~$94M (Delinea, CBInsights); StrongDM raised ~$54M separately — acquisition terms undisclosed
funding.notes: Mature PE-backed company. Not a startup — enterprise product with 1,100+ employees.

contacts.notes: Vocal on AI agent authorization. Quoted in acquisition announcement.

pp_fit.feature: Immutable action-time receipt layer on top of runtime authorization
pp_fit.integration_complexity: medium — enterprise platform, REST APIs likely available; partnership/OEM path more realistic than direct SDK drop-in
pp_fit.urgency: high — just completed acquisition to address exact AI agent governance gap; CEO actively narrating the problem space
pp_fit.strategic_angle: PP fills the gap Delinea/StrongDM explicitly leaves open: they do authorization decisions (allow/deny), PP creates the cryptographic proof of what the agent was authorized to do vs. what it actually did. Complementary, not competitive. PARTNERSHIP play, not a customer play — PP could be the immutable audit receipt layer embedded in their platform.

notes: STRATEGIC ALLY. Partnership play, not a customer. They do the access decision; PP does the receipt. Delinea's enterprise customer base (F500, finance, government) is PP's dream market. Approach: position PP as the audit-receipt layer Delinea/StrongDM sells to their existing customers as an add-on. Art Gilliland is the right first contact — he's publicly narrating the exact problem.
